records.name: Olney Culture Lab
records.summary: A CultureTrust project that celebrates the mix of cultures in the Olney neighborhood through festivals, a podcast, and a video series. Most people take part by coming to the events.
records.what_you_do: Attend the Olney Youth Arts Festival or A Taste of Olney, listen to the Audio Olney podcast, or give a donation. The site does not say how to volunteer.

schedule.text: Events are posted on the site calendar. The 2026 Olney Youth Arts Festival and A Taste of Olney are listed for October 2026.

cost.text: Event prices are not listed on the site. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Check the site calendar and come to the next festival or event. Sign up on the Get Updates form to hear about new dates.
first_step.basis: Events are public and listed on the website with a sign-up for updates

records.notes: No address, email or phone is published on the home page. The Contact page was linked but not read. Volunteer roles are not described.

records.name: PB&J of CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: A Sunday cooking program in Kensington for teens ages 12 to 19. Teens learn to cook, plan meals, and build life skills, and they are paid for taking part.
records.what_you_do: Teens come to the Sunday cooking program and learn cooking, nutrition, and safety, with links to local businesses and internships. Volunteers and donors can use the Get Involved and Donate pages.

schedule.text: Sundays. The site gives no start time.

cost.text: No program fee is listed. Teens are paid for taking part.

first_step.how: Open the Get Cooking page on the site to sign up, then come to the Sunday program.
first_step.basis: The site invites teens to come every Sunday and links to a sign-up page

records.notes: The site is current in its invitations, but the newest dated item is a 2023 news link to an article about a November pilot. Nothing dated since then was found, so confirm the Sunday program is running before listing it as active. Contact details are as published on the site. The page does not say which parts are for teens and which are for volunteers.

records.name: Rittenhouse Sound (Philadelphia Chapter SPEBSQSA)
records.summary: Philadelphia's lower-voice a cappella chorus. Singers rehearse each week, perform in concerts, and take part in chapter quartet contests.
records.what_you_do: Audition to join the chorus and sing at weekly Tuesday rehearsals. Visitors can watch the group's recordings or attend a performance.

schedule.text: Weekly rehearsals on Tuesdays at 7:15 pm at the Philadelphia Ethical Society.

cost.text: No dues or rehearsal fees are published.

first_step.how: Look for the audition notice on the site, or use the contact page to ask about the next audition.
first_step.basis: Joining needs an audition, and the site does not say what the process is like before that

records.notes: The batch lists this group under the SPEBSQSA chapter name. The website calls itself Rittenhouse Sound. The site lists a weekly rehearsal schedule and auditions, but its Latest News section has no dated items, so status is probably_active. No street address or contact email appears on the home page; the Contact page was linked but not read.

records.name: Philadelphia Jazz Legacy Project
records.summary: Five Philadelphia jazz groups working together to collect, save, and share the city's jazz history. It also records life-story interviews with musicians and neighbors.
records.what_you_do: Send photos, concert programs, clippings, or recordings from Philadelphia jazz history through the submission form, or help the project record interviews.

schedule.text: No schedule published. A talk and listening session with the archivist was posted in September 2026.

cost.text: No fees are listed for contributing. The site has donate and shop links.

first_step.how: Fill out the submission form on the site to offer materials, or call the project director to talk about a donation of materials.
first_step.basis: The submission form is public and anyone can offer materials

records.notes: Phone number is the Project Director's, as published. The email address is obscured on the page. The archive is housed at the Charles L. Blockson Collection at Temple University. The five partner organizations are not named on the page, so they are not listed as leads.

records.name: PlayPenn
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that helps writers develop new plays through classes, workshops, and a yearly new play conference.
records.what_you_do: Take a class for playwrights and theater makers, apply for an artistic program, or go to a public event.

schedule.text: Fall classes start October 1 (year not stated). The 2026 New Play Development Conference schedule is posted as a download.

cost.text: Class fees and ticket prices are not listed. A refund policy and financial aid information are linked.

first_step.how: Browse the classes and the conference schedule on the site, read the financial aid information, then sign up.
first_step.basis: Classes and events are listed publicly with a sign-up route

records.notes: The only year on the site is 2026, attached to the conference. Fall class dates have no year. The published street address is a mailing address (box number 22606), so it is not recorded as a meeting place. Status is probably_active from the 2026 conference and fall classes, not from a dated news item.

records.name: Practice Space Collective
records.summary: A theater collective that makes plays, podcasts, and performance projects about social and economic change, including a project on Philadelphia schools.
records.what_you_do: The home page lists its current projects and an Offerings section. What joining or attending looks like is not spelled out on the page read.

first_step.how: Use the contact page to ask what the Offerings section includes and whether new people can take part.
first_step.basis: The page lists offerings but the way in is not described

records.notes: The site loads but shows no dates. Status is probably_active only because it is a working site with no dates. The Offerings and Contact pages were not read, so the way in is not confirmed. No address or contact details were found.

records.name: PRISM Quartet
records.summary: A saxophone quartet that commissions and records new music, tours, and runs an education institute for composers and players.
records.what_you_do: Attend a concert, join the mailing list and mark interest in volunteering, or take part in the PRISM Quartet Institute programs for composers and players.

schedule.text: Concerts are listed on the Concerts page, including October 27 and 28 performances at two Michigan universities (year not shown). A JazzTimes blog post is dated September 30, 2026.

cost.text: No ticket prices or program fees are published.

first_step.how: Go to a concert on the Concerts page, or sign up for the mailing list and mark interest in volunteering.
first_step.basis: Concerts are public and the volunteer interest form is open to anyone

records.notes: The pages read do not state a Philadelphia base, so the Philadelphia link comes from the Cultural Fund list. Confirm the group serves Philadelphia before it goes live; if not, change the verdict to out_of_area. The Institute is the most local-facing part.

records.name: Prismatic Arts Ensemble
records.summary: A Philadelphia classical music group that stages concerts with bold programming, immersive staging, and storytelling.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to one of its concerts or cabarets, or donate. The site does not list classes, auditions or volunteer roles.

schedule.text: The only event listed is a Pride cabaret on June 26, 2026, at 8:00 pm, part of the Philly Pride Arts Festival.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not listed on the page read.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the next listed show through the ticket link on the site.
first_step.basis: Shows are ticketed and open to the public, though the site lists no class or volunteer route

records.notes: Only one event is listed and it is from June 2026, so the group is active within 12 months but has no upcoming dates on the page. Address not published.

records.name: Philadelphia Latino Arts & Film Festival
records.summary: A community film and arts festival that shows Latino films and runs a weekly screening club in Center City.
records.what_you_do: Come to the People's Cinema Club screenings on Tuesdays, go to the festival, or volunteer or intern. Filmmakers can submit films.

schedule.text: People's Cinema Club screenings every Tuesday at 6:30 pm in Center City. The 2027 festival runs May 30 to July 4, 2027.

cost.text: Screenings are sold through Eventbrite. Prices are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the next Tuesday People's Cinema Club screening, or use the Volunteer or Intern page to offer help.
first_step.basis: Screenings are public and listed every week

records.notes: A program of CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia. Address, email and phone are not published on the page read. The Film Submissions and Volunteer pages were linked but not read.

records.name: Philadelphia Scenic Works
records.summary: A nonprofit scene shop that builds sets and scenery for arts groups, and trains people who want backstage careers. It runs a free High School Tech Theatre Club.
records.what_you_do: Join the free High School Tech Theatre Club, take training in backstage work, or join the mailing list to hear about openings.

schedule.text: The High School Tech Theatre Club is described as back, with a sign-up form. Meeting times are not listed.

cost.text: The High School Tech Theatre Club is free. Other training costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Fill out the High School Tech Theatre Club sign-up form on the site.
first_step.basis: The club is free and has a public sign-up form

records.notes: The newest post is dated 01/18 with no year. It is about columns for the 2026 Philadelphia Flower Show, so 2026-01 is inferred, not read. Address and contact details are not on the page read; the Contact page was not read.

records.name: Philadelphia Wind Symphony
records.summary: A volunteer band of about 51 woodwind, brass, and percussion players who perform about six concerts a season across Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Play in the band as a substitute on wind, brass, or percussion, or go to a concert. Donations and newsletter sign-up are also open.

schedule.text: Concerts run October to June. The October family concert, Trick or Treat, was free at the Kroc Center on October 31 at 11 am (2025, year inferred from the event link).

cost.text: The October family concert is free. Other ticket prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Apply as a substitute on the site if you play wind, brass, or percussion, or go to a free October concert to hear the band first.
first_step.basis: Regular seats were closed for the 2026 to 2027 season and substitutes need to apply, so the way in is not open to walk-ins

records.notes: Mailing address is a PO Box, 42224, Philadelphia, PA 19101, so it is not recorded as a location. The 2025 year for the October concert is inferred from the event link, not stated on the page. Auditions for 2026 to 2027 are closed, so check the site before the next season.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Dance Fest
records.summary: A festival that brings young dancers together for three days of master classes and a chance to perform. It runs in Philadelphia and in the Lehigh Valley.
records.what_you_do: Dance companies apply through an online form. Dancers take four to six master classes and perform one piece of up to 4.5 minutes. Scholarship classes are held at each festival.

schedule.text: Philadelphia festival March 19 to 21, 2027 at Drexel University. Lehigh Valley festival May 14 to 16, 2027 at Muhlenberg College. Each has a Friday option, Saturday classes from 9 am to 6 pm, and Sunday classes and performances.

cost.text: 2027 prices: $50 company application fee, $115 per student for the Philadelphia festival, $65 class-only fee for the Lehigh Valley festival, or $200 for both.

first_step.how: A dance company fills in the online company application form. Dancers then join through their company.
first_step.basis: Dancers enter through a company application and pay fees, and the page does not describe an open sign-up for individual dancers

records.notes: Every dated item on the site is in 2027, so status is probably_active rather than active. Dance interest uses dance_company as the closest tag. Address not published beyond the two host campuses. The page gives no volunteer or audience sign-up route.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Orchestra Music Institute
records.summary: The music school of the Philadelphia Youth Orchestra. It gives music education to young players through auditioned ensembles and lessons.
records.what_you_do: Audition for a youth ensemble or study an instrument with the institute. Anyone can attend the public concerts or sign up for the newsletter.

schedule.text: Concerts are listed at Kimmel Center venues and the Please Touch Museum. A youth jazz orchestra performs December 5, 2026 at 2 pm at the Please Touch Museum. The program schedule is not on the page.

cost.text: Tuition, audition and ticket prices are not published on the page read.

first_step.how: Open the auditions page on the site and contact the institute to ask about the next audition date.
first_step.basis: Ensembles need auditions and the page does not say how enrollment works

records.notes: The only dated item is a scheduled December 2026 concert, so status is probably_active. The auditions page was linked but not read. Mailing address is P.O. Box 41810, Philadelphia, PA 19101-1810, not recorded as a location. Phone and email are as published.

records.name: Philly Dance Share
records.summary: A volunteer-run dance collective that offers affordable weekly classes for adult dancers at every level.
records.what_you_do: Take a weekly class from the class schedule, teach a class, or get involved by emailing the group.

schedule.text: Weekly classes. The current calendar runs October 8 to 24, 2026, with the full schedule on the class schedule page.

cost.text: The group describes its classes as affordable. Prices are not listed on the page read.

first_step.how: Pick a class on the class schedule page and go. Email the group to ask about prices and where classes meet.
first_step.basis: Classes are for dancers of all levels and the schedule is posted publicly

records.notes: Meeting address is not published. Classes are listed through October 24, 2026. The social_dance tag is the closest fit for a general adult class collective.

notes: 18 groups in batch. Each was checked against its own site with WebFetch, except the two marked rate-limited. One WebSearch used for the Clef Club address and history, since its own site returned 409. Budget not exhausted: 1 of 2 searches, 16 of 60 fetches. Two groups (Private Theater, Project Moshen) are held back because no page could be read. Several groups list only future-dated events, so their status is probably_active rather than active. Scheduled items with no past date were not treated as proof of activity. Wind Symphony and Scenic Works had years inferred from event links or post dates; those are noted per record. PB&J is the main case to check by hand: its Sunday program is invited on the site, but the newest dated item is from 2023-12. Nothing was copied from any source; all summaries are written fresh.
